title: Arc Institute State: First-Generation Virtual Cell Predicts Genetic and Drug Perturbations Across Unseen Contexts
whyItMatters: Trained on >100M perturbed cells and 167M observational human cells, Arc Institute’s State improved perturbation discrimination by >50% and differentially expressed gene identification >2× across unseen cell contexts.
summary: Released on June 27, 2025 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.26.661135) by Abhinav K. Adduri, Dhruv Gautam, Beatrice Bevilacqua, Hani Goodarzi, Yusuf H. Roohani, and colleagues at the Arc Institute, State is a first-generation multiscale virtual cell architecture built to predict single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic, signaling, and chemical perturbations while preserving cell-to-cell heterogeneity. State pairs a cell embedding model trained on 167 million observational human cells with a set-to-set state-transition transformer trained on over 100 million perturbed cells across 70 cellular contexts (including Tahoe-100M). Evaluated using the accompanying Cell-Eval benchmark, State improved perturbation effect discrimination by over 50% across major datasets, achieved more than 2-fold higher accuracy identifying true differentially expressed genes across genetic and drug perturbations, and transferred to novel cell types where zero perturbations were seen during training.
technicalHighlights: Combines a 167M-cell observational embedding model with a state-transition model trained on >100M perturbed cells across 70 cellular contexts.
Improved perturbation discrimination by >50% and achieved >2× accuracy identifying true differentially expressed genes across genetic, cytokine, and chemical perturbations.
Predicts strong cell-type-specific perturbation responses (including cell survival) in novel cell contexts with zero perturbation training data.
caveats: bioRxiv preprint under active peer review; virtual-cell perturbation prediction on completely unseen drug mechanisms remains noisy relative to experimental Perturb-seq.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrates that scaling set-level transition transformers over >100M perturbed cells unlocks cross-context virtual-cell response prediction.
scoreRationale.ripple: Accelerates in silico target prioritization, drug-mechanism screening, and the broader virtual-cell ecosystem with open weights and Cell-Eval benchmarks.
scoreRationale.verification: Evaluated across multi-million-cell genetic and chemical Perturb-seq benchmarks via Cell-Eval, though formal journal peer review is pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Simulates thousands of candidate genetic and chemical perturbations across unseen cell types computationally before running wet-lab screens.
